pr.title: Fix cycle error only occurring with -Zdump-mir
pr.description:
fixes #134205

During mir dumping, we evaluate static items to render their allocations. If a static item refers to itself, its own MIR will have a reference to itself, so during mir dumping we end up evaluating the static again, causing us to try to build MIR again (mir dumping happens during MIR building).

Thus I disabled evaluation of statics during MIR dumps in case the MIR body isn't far enough along yet to be able to be guaranteed cycle free.
pr.author: oli-obk

issues.title: `-Zdump-mir` introduces cycle in static containing static reference
issues.body:
```rust
// src/lib.rs

pub struct Thing {
    pub next: &'static Thing,
}

pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
```

```console
$ cargo clean
$ RUSTFLAGS=-Zdump-mir= cargo build

error[E0391]: cycle detected when evaluating initializer of static `THING`
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
note: ...which requires caching mir of `THING` for CTFE...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
note: ...which requires elaborating drops for `THING`...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
note: ...which requires borrow-checking `THING`...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
note: ...which requires promoting constants in MIR for `THING`...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
note: ...which requires const checking `THING`...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
note: ...which requires building MIR for `THING`...
 --> src/lib.rs:7:1
  |
7 | pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = note: ...which again requires evaluating initializer of static `THING`, completing the cycle
  = note: cycle used when running analysis passes on this crate
  = note: see https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/overview.html#queries and https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/query.html for more information

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0391`.
error: could not compile `repro` (lib) due to 1 previous error
```

The error does not occur if you build without `-Zdump-mir` first.

```console
$ cargo clean
$ cargo build
$ RUSTFLAGS=-Zdump-mir= cargo build
```

processing.reason: The PR fixes a `-Zdump-mir` pretty-printing issue where rendering MIR allocations calls `eval_static_initializer` on a self-referential static during MIR building, causing an E0391 query cycle. This is not a miscompilation or value transformation: normal program evaluation is unchanged before and after the fix, and the defect manifests only as a dump-time diagnostic cycle. Modeling the old behavior as a recursive static-initializer evaluator would not pass Miri, while any invented function pair returning different values (e.g., presence/absence of an error flag or allocation bytes) would be an arbitrary rewrite unrelated to the actual historical semantics. Therefore no source-grounded pair with identical inputs, both passing Miri, and different defined original/transformed results exists for this PR.

analysis.summary: -Zdump-mir pretty-printing of MIR allocations unconditionally evaluated referenced static initializers. For a static that refers to itself, rendering the dump re-entered MIR building for that same static and produced an E0391 query cycle even though normal compilation succeeds. The fix suppresses static-initializer evaluation during early MIR dump phases when the dumped body is itself a const/static initializer, emitting only the static's def path instead of its bytes. The mir-opt expectations for PromoteTemps and SimplifyCfg dumps changed accordingly (allocation contents disappear).
analysis.originalLogic: In `write_allocations` (compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/pretty.rs), for `Some(GlobalAlloc::Static(did)) if !tcx.is_foreign_item(did)`, the printer called `tcx.eval_static_initializer(did)`. On `Ok(alloc)` it wrote `" (static: {}, "` followed by `write_allocation_track_relocs(w, alloc)` (the static's bytes/relocations); on `Err(_)` it wrote `" (static: {}, error during initializer evaluation)"`. Thus printing a MIR body evaluated any referenced static's initializer to render its allocation contents.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to evaluate the referenced static initializer unconditionally during MIR dumping, without checking how far along the current MIR body was or whether the body is a const/static initializer. Because MIR dumping happens during MIR building, a self-referential static's own MIR contains a reference to itself; evaluating it again mid-dump re-entered MIR building for the same static and completed a query cycle (E0391) under `-Zdump-mir`, even though the same crate compiles normally without `-Zdump-mir`. The corrected transformation gates evaluation: when `body.phase <= MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::PostCleanup)` and `tcx.hir().body_const_context(body.source.def_id()).is_some()`, it writes only `" (static: <def_path>)"` and skips `eval_static_initializer`; otherwise it still evaluates and prints bytes or the error marker.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust crates dumped with `-Zdump-mir` that contain static/const initializer bodies referencing statics, especially self-referential or mutually recursive statics (e.g. `pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };` or a static initialized through a const fn returning a reference to another static). Relevant dumps are early-phase (`body.phase <= MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::PostCleanup)`) const-context bodies and promoted-constant dumps produced by PromoteTemps/SimplifyCfg. To build two programs differing only in the transformation, use the same crate/static definition and vary whether the dump runs while the static body is still early/in a const context (evaluation suppressed) versus a later non-const-context body (evaluation retained); the key input feature is the self/mutual static reference, not any MIR value assignment.
analysis.trigger: Rendering a MIR dump for a static/const initializer body at or before the PostCleanup runtime phase, where the body contains an allocation reference to a static whose initializer evaluates back to the same in-progress MIR body (direct self-reference or mutual recursion through a const fn). `-Zdump-mir` must be enabled so that dumping occurs during MIR building.
preconditions: Compilation runs with -Zdump-mir (dump occurs during MIR building).
The dumped MIR body is a const context: `tcx.hir().body_const_context(body.source.def_id()).is_some()`.
An allocation in the body references a non-foreign static, and evaluating that static re-enters the same/in-progress MIR body (cyclic static).
Normal compilation without -Zdump-mir succeeds; the cycle is dump-induced.
pitfalls: Do not conclude that the static is genuinely ill-formed or that CTFE finds a real cycle; the reported cycle is an artifact of dump-time evaluation and disappears without -Zdump-mir.

Do not keep expecting full allocation bytes in mir-opt dumps for early const-context bodies; the fix intentionally emits only `(static: <def_path>)`, so PromoteTemps/SimplifyCfg expectations lose `ALLOC0 (... size ... )` contents.
The gate requires BOTH the early-phase condition and the const-context condition; applying only one is not equivalent to the historical/desired behavior.
This is a pretty-printer/dump-path correctness issue, not a change to actual static evaluation or to the PromoteTemps/SimplifyCfg transformations themselves.
The old `Err` path already printed an error marker; the new early path must not accidentally report an evaluation error, since no evaluation is attempted.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt regression test (tests/mir-opt/building/dump_mir_cycle.rs) with a directly self-referential static and a mutually recursive static reached through a const fn, and assert the dump contains `alloc... (static: THING)` / `(static: MUTUALLY_RECURSIVE)` without byte contents. Exercise both the direct and mutual-recursion variants and call the const fn from `main` so optimized MIR is also generated. Update existing PromoteTemps/SimplifyCfg dump expectations to the shortened `ALLOC0 (static: Y)` form. Run with -Zdump-mir to ensure no E0391 cycle, and compare against a build without -Zdump-mir to confirm normal compilation is unchanged.
evidence: During mir dumping, we evaluate static items to render their allocations. If a static item refers to itself, its own MIR will have a reference to itself, so during mir dumping we end up evaluating the static again, causing us to try to build MIR again (mir dumping happens during MIR building).
Thus I disabled evaluation of statics during MIR dumps in case the MIR body isn't far enough along yet to be able to be guaranteed cycle free.
// Statics may be cyclic and evaluating them too early
// in the MIR pipeline may cause cycle errors even though
pub static THING: Thing = Thing { next: &THING };
pub static MUTUALLY_RECURSIVE: Thing = Thing { next: thing() };
The error does not occur if you build without `-Zdump-mir` first.
